Hannah / Ben —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can scope the evaluation: 

- Our primary goal is to validate real-world unit economics vs the hyperscaler-managed endpoints (we're currently testing with Hyperscale-A and Hyperscale-B). Key numbers we need: per-1M token cost under our workload, tail latency at p95/p99 for 1–8 concurrent inference streams, and impact of batching + KV cache hit rates.
- We're especially sensitive to cold-start behavior and how model fallbacks (smaller model variants) affect quality and cost.
- Security/compliance: we'll want evidence of data isolation and audit logs for the trial — we'll send a short questionnaire separately.

Can you confirm Redwood can run a short probe (1M tokens synthetic + customer sample) and provide a runbook for the tests you propose? Also, please attach any non-disclosure paperwork so procurement can get this moving.

Jane — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the NDA. Attached is a draft probe worksheet that outlines the tests we recommend and the data we'll capture: per-1M token cost (hosted vs dedicated baseline), batching sensitivity, and cache-hit modeling. High-level responses to your asks below.

What we can run for the 1–2 week probe
- Synthetic workload (1M tokens canonical run) + a 200k token run with your redacted sample prompts.
- Measurements: token split (prompt v. completion), p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU-utilization, and effective tokens/sec.
- Batching matrix: single-request, small batch (N=4–8), and aggressive batch (N=16+) with corresponding latency vs throughput curves.
- KV prefix cache: we'll sweep cache hit rates (0%, 30%, 60%, 90%) to estimate cost deltas.
- Hyperscaler comparisons: we'll run the same canonical suite against our hosted endpoint and a comparable Hyperscale-A managed endpoint you provided (same model family) — we normalize for batch size and sequence length.

Key differentiators you'll see from Redwood during the probe
- Unified routing: we can route by latency/cost regionally and automatically fall back to smaller variants if SLOs are missed. That reduces tail-costs vs naive single-endpoint routing.
- Cache-aware billing model: we show effective tokens billed after prefix/KV hits rather than raw emitted tokens. This typically shows a 10–30% unit-cost advantage on chat-heavy workloads vs hyperscaler baselines.
- Production runtime features: continuous batching, KV cache hot-paths, and quantization-friendly kernels that preserve throughput at low-latency windows.

Next steps / asks
1) Sign NDA (received) and confirm preferred window for the probe (we suggest Wed 12/16 — Fri 12/18).
2) Tell us whether you prefer a hosted Redwood sandbox or a temporary Dedicated pool / Private VPC for performance parity testing. Dedicated/VPC gives more stable p99s but takes slightly longer to provision.
3) Share a 200–500 prompt sample (redacted) and indicate your typical sequence lengths.

I've attached the probe worksheet (redwood-infer-econ-probe.xlsx) and a short runbook draft (runbook-perf-tests.md). Ben and Marcus are looped in to handle the lab work and artefacts.

Cheers,
Hannah Schmitt
